summary: Cyril Henry Philips was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Liverpool and SOAS University of London. He served as Director of SOAS from 1957 and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of London from 1972 to 1976.

Cyrus Stearns works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA under Turrell V. Wylie and his PhD under Leonard van der Kuijp at the University of Washington, also studying under several traditional teachers, and became a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.

Cécile Ducher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD under Matthew T. Kapstein at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where she subsequently held an appointment as a research fellow.

D. C. Lau was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied under Xu Dishan at The University of Hong Kong and later attended the University of Glasgow. He held appointments at SOAS, University College London, the University of London, and CUHK.
D. C. Sarasvati was an Indology scholar who studied under V. Raghavan. Sarasvati held an appointment at the University of Madras as a Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant from 1964 to 1965.
D. Dennis Hudson was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. From approximately 1970 to 2004, he taught at Smith College as a professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies.

D. L. Narasimhachar was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, from around 1925 to 1929 and served on the faculty at the University of Mysore from approximately 1932 to 1962.

D. N. Shukla was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed a D.Litt. at the University of Lucknow under K. A. Subramania Iyer and held an attested post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University in 1958.

D. Neil Schmid specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies under Victor H. Mair at the University of Pennsylvania, and also studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Waseda University.

D. Phillip Stanley specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano at the University of Virginia and served as an associate professor at Naropa University and Co-Director of the Nitartha Institute.

D. R. Shackleton Bailey worked in Tibetology, Indology, and classics. Educated at Cambridge, he held fellowships and posts at Cambridge (1944–1968), and was later a professor at the University of Michigan (1968–1976, 1988–2002) and Harvard (1975–1988).

Dagfinn Føllesdal was a philosopher and linguist. He studied at the University of Oslo and completed his PhD at Harvard under Willard Van Orman Quine. He taught at Harvard, Stanford University (1968–2011), and the University of Oslo.
Dagmar Schwerk works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her studies at the University of Hamburg from approximately 2012 to 2017 under doctoral supervisor Dorji Wangchuk.

Daiei Kaneko was a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher. He studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and at Otani University, where he later taught from roughly 1916 to 1928, in addition to holding a post at Toyo University.

Daijo Tokiwa was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora, later serving as a professor at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University.

Daiju Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from roughly 1996 to 2007. His attested positions in 2015 include part-time lecturer at Taisho University and full-time lecturer in sectarian studies at Chisan Denpōin.

Dainin Katagiri was a Buddhist studies figure who trained under Eko Hashimoto and Daicho Hayashi at Eihei-ji and studied at Komazawa University. He served as a priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission and as interim abbot at San Francisco Zen Center.

Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied under Kosen Imakita, Sōen Shaku, and Paul Carus. He held professorships at Gakushuin, the University of Tokyo, Otani University (1921–1960), and Columbia University (1952–1957).

Daishun Ueyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied under Akira Fujieda. He served at Ryukoku University as an assistant professor around 1970–1976 and became its president in 1983.

Daito Shimaji was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Ryukoku and Toyo universities, he taught Indian philosophy at the University of Tokyo in 1923, and taught at Toyo, Komazawa, and Rissho universities in the 1920s.
